title: AWS Retail Store Sample App
summary: A five-service retail application on Amazon ECS: Aurora, DynamoDB, OpenSearch, ElastiCache and Amazon MQ behind an Application Load Balancer. StackToIT read the ECS Terraform estate and wrote a STACKIT migration package.

source.registry_modules: 13 registry modules resolved by OpenTofu (terraform-aws-modules, cloudposse)
source.note: The estate was assessed exactly as published upstream: nothing in it was edited. It ships no .terraform.lock.hcl. Because of that the source provider is UNPINNED and the OpenTofu validation of the source did not run, even with a provider mirror prepared beforehand: StackToIT validates a source only against the provider versions its lock file records, and will not pick one for it.
source.description: The retail-store-sample-app by AWS Containers is a sample retail application: five services (ui, catalog, carts, checkout, orders) on Amazon ECS behind an Application Load Balancer, with Aurora (catalog, orders), DynamoDB (carts), OpenSearch (catalog), ElastiCache (checkout) and Amazon MQ as managed dependencies in one VPC. The estate assessed is its terraform/ecs/default root module and the local terraform/lib modules it calls.
source.attribution: The source estate is the retail-store-sample-app published by AWS under MIT-0.

run.mode: online (default options; a local OpenTofu provider mirror with hashicorp/aws 5.100.0 was prepared beforehand as the console suggests; prices from the local price cache retrieved 2026-10-26)
run.command_note: Run from the vendored copy of the upstream repository. A local OpenTofu provider mirror (hashicorp/aws 5.100.0, the version the constraints resolve to) was prepared first with `tofu providers mirror`, as the first run's console suggested; the source validation still did not run because the source has no lock file. The output directory is this example's output/ folder, unchanged.

key_findings.title: Nothing is DIRECT
key_findings.text: All 44 present units need at least a reconfiguration: 34 RECONFIGURE, 9 REPLATFORM (ECS → SKE, Aurora → MariaDB/PostgreSQL Flex, OpenSearch), 1 REDESIGN (DynamoDB has no STACKIT counterpart; MongoDB Flex or PostgreSQL JSONB are the named options).

key_findings.title: The source provider is unpinned, so the source was not validated
key_findings.text: The upstream estate commits no .terraform.lock.hcl. StackToIT caps every unit at MEDIUM confidence, marks none automation-eligible, and does not run OpenTofu validation on the source, with or without a provider mirror, because no lock file states which provider version to validate against. It names the two remedies (commit a lock file with aws 5.100.0, or raise the constraint to ~> 6.0 and lock 6.67.0); only a lock file and a source validation show that either works.

key_findings.title: Catalog is deployment-blocked
key_findings.text: The catalog service depends on OpenSearch 3.3; the STACKIT region offers version 2. The draft stays blocked until a test shows the application works on that version or an architecture decision is recorded.

key_findings.title: Four STACKIT API steps wait for an opt-in
key_findings.text: The draft gives the four data services (Aurora → MariaDB and PostgreSQL Flex, Amazon MQ → RabbitMQ, ElastiCache → Valkey) a public STACKIT endpoint limited by an access list, where the source kept them private. That widening is not carried out by default: their steps wait until a Security Architect accepts the exposure or chooses another way in. This is the first required action of the run.

key_findings.title: Two replacements wait for a person's choice
key_findings.text: The SKE cluster that replaces the ECS services and the MongoDB Flex instance that replaces the DynamoDB tables are proposed alternatives. Their OpenTofu steps wait until a person chooses how the container runtime and the NoSQL tables move, so 29 of the 49 automated steps are free of decisions, against 31 in the previous version. That is a correctness gain, not a regression: the draft does not write a replacement nobody has chosen.

key_findings.title: No cost comparison is stated
key_findings.text: The source does not name its AWS region, so no AWS price was fetched. 5 of 14 STACKIT lines are priced (878.34 EUR partial, list prices); the report refuses to call a one-sided subtotal a saving.

key_findings.title: The security-widening check stays open
key_findings.text: 11 of the 12 global checks pass; the one that stays open is that no rule, route or role assignment allows more than the source did. The five ECS task roles become STACKIT project role assignments whose roles a person fills, and what a STACKIT project role allows is not stated in any public source, so StackToIT does not call the access equal.

publication.outside_manifest_note: review/ is the customer's answer area the run writes beside its files; it is excluded from the manifest by design. manifest.json lists every other file.
publication.statement: The output folder is published exactly as StackToIT wrote it. No file was removed, edited or redacted; stacktoit verify passes on the published copy.

case_study.lede: Explore how StackToIT analyzed the AWS Retail Store Sample App and generated a structured migration assessment, proposed STACKIT infrastructure, architecture diagrams and a detailed migration plan.
